# Optimal Transit pitches Kraaken floating data center than can generate power and provide clean drinking water

Project sounds ambitious, but is apparently based on proven technologies

August 13, 2026

By
: Matthew Gooding 

Self-powered floating data centers that can also act as power plants and water treatment facilities are being pitched by a new company, Optimal Transit.

The firm, a joint venture between naval systems developer InMar Technologies and power technology firm OptiFuel, has unveiled its Kraaken range of data centers, which it says will offer capacity of between 10MW and 100MW.

A second iteration of the design will add power generation and water treatment capabilities, alongside 60MW of compute space. Optimal Transit says this will make it ideal for areas hit by natural disasters.

Rather than relying on grid energy, Kraaken will apparently generate its own continuous electrical power by “combining the thermal energy naturally stored in the ocean with waste heat produced by the data center itself.” This is done using the company’s patented multi-stage Digital Ocean Thermal (DOT) engine.

## Story

Hanwha Ocean Unveils 60MW Floating Data Center < Defense·Energy < 기사본문 - The Elec Inc.

## Offshore platform generates power, uses seawater cooling and offers modular configurations

- EunGyu Kim 
- Published 2026.09.14 07:26
- Reply 0

 

A model of Hanwha Ocean's FDC.

Hanwha Ocean will unveil its first 60-megawatt (MW) floating data center (FDC), developed to address growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers.

Hanwha Ocean said on Sept. 13 that it will showcase its internally developed 60MW FDC model at Gastech 2026, an energy exhibition opening in Thailand on Sept. 14.

An FDC houses a data center on a floating offshore structure. It can generate its own power at sea and use seawater for cooling, helping address challenges faced by land-based data centers in securing power and sites and managing cooling.

Hanwha Ocean has adopted a modular design for the FDC. Power generation and supply methods, server types and data center capacity can be configured according to the installation location and customer requirements. The company recently received Approval in Principle (AiP) from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) for the conceptual design of the 60MW FDC.
